title: Symmetric blowup along the closure of one nodal point
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-kun-separably-closed] and $V\subseteq K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$, meaning that for $z\in K^\times$ either $z$ or $z^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Suppose the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}V$ and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-curve here is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with pure one-dimensional fibres [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], without any separatedness or properness assumption. A curve is semistable if every nonsmooth point of every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $f:X\to S$ be a semistable $S$-curve with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $J=\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega^1_{X/S})$ and $N=V_X(J)$, the first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme], and suppose its underlying set is finite. Fix any point $z\in N$, put $s_0=z|_S$, and let $C=\overline{\{z\}}\subseteq X$ be its topological closure. The set $C$ is contained in $|N|$. There exist a nonzero element $\pi\in V$, an open neighbourhood $W$ of all of $C$ in $X$, and a finite affine open cover $W=\bigcup_\alpha W_\alpha$ with the following properties. The vanishing set $V_S(\pi)$ is exactly the closure of $\{s_0\}$ in $S$, and $|N|\cap W\cap f^{-1}V_S(\pi)=C$. Each $W_\alpha$ maps into an open $S_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}R_\alpha$ of $S$, with $R_\alpha$ a localization of $V$. There are $0\ne a_\alpha\in R_\alpha$, an etale cover $T_\alpha\to W_\alpha$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and an etale $R_\alpha$-morphism $T_\alpha\to M_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}R_\alpha[u,v]/(uv-a_\alpha)$, such that $J\mathcal O_{T_\alpha}=(u,v)\mathcal O_{T_\alpha}$ and $b_\alpha=a_\alpha/\pi^2\in R_\alpha$. The ideals $J|_W+(\pi)$ on $W$ and $\mathcal O_{X\setminus C}$ on $X\setminus C$ agree on their overlap, so define a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$.
The blowup $q:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_I X\to X$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], is an isomorphism on $X\setminus C$ and on the whole generic fibre, and $X^+$ is a reduced semistable $S$-curve. The blowup is locally covered by the rings $A[I/g]\subseteq A_g$ for generators $g$ of $I$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Its pullback to $T_\alpha$ is the etale pullback of the blowup of $(u,v,\pi)$ on $M_\alpha$. The three standard chart rings of that model blowup are
$$R_\alpha[u,p]/(up-\pi),\qquad R_\alpha[r,t]/(rt-b_\alpha),\qquad R_\alpha[v,h]/(vh-\pi),$$
with maps to $M_\alpha$ given respectively by $v=\pi b_\alpha p$, by $u=\pi r,v=\pi t$, and by $u=\pi b_\alpha h$. For every $s\in S$, every reduced irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $(X^+)_s$ is smooth over $\kappa(s)$ at every point that maps into $C$. If $E\hookrightarrow X$ is any closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] disjoint from $C$, its inverse image is isomorphic to $E$.
